title.zh: 卷四十六 列傳第四十 胡僧祐 徐文盛 杜崱 兄岸 弟幼安 兄子龕 陰子春
title.en: Volume 46: Hu Sengyou; Xu Wensheng; Du Ze; Du An; Du You'an; Du Kan; Yin Zichun
title.raw: 卷四十六 列傳第四十 胡僧祐 徐文盛 杜崱 兄岸 弟幼安 兄子龕 陰子春 Volume 46: Hu Sengyou; Xu Wensheng; Du Ze; Du An; Du You'an; Du Kan; Yin Zichun

sentences.zh: 梁書卷第四十六 列傳第四十

translations.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 46, Biography 40
translations.idiomatic: Book of Liang, Volume 46, Biography 40

sentences.zh: 胡僧祐 徐文盛 杜崱 兄岸 弟幼安 兄子龕 陰子春

translations.literal: Hu Sengyou, Xu Wensheng, Du Ze, elder brother An, younger brother You'an, elder brother's son Kan, Yin Zichun
translations.idiomatic: Hu Sengyou; Xu Wensheng; Du Ze; Du An; Du You'an; Du Kan; Yin Zichun

sentences.zh: 晚事世祖，爲鎮西錄事參軍。

translations.literal: In his later years he served Emperor Shizu as staff recorder in the Pacifying West headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served Shizu as recorder on the Pacifying West staff.

sentences.zh: 侯景亂，西沮蠻反，世祖令僧祐討之，使盡誅其渠帥，僧祐諫，忤旨下獄。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled, the Western Ju barbarians revolted; Shizu ordered Sengyou to suppress them and to execute all their chieftains; Sengyou remonstrated and, defying the edict, was thrown into prison.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled the Western Ju rose; Shizu ordered Sengyou to put them down and kill every chieftain; Sengyou remonstrated, offended the throne, and was jailed.

sentences.zh: 大寶二年，侯景寇荊陝，圍王僧辯于巴陵，世祖乃引僧祐於獄，拜爲假節、武猛將軍，封新市縣侯，令赴援。

translations.literal: In the second year of Great Treasure, when Hou Jing raided Jing and Shan and besieged Wang Sengbian at Baling, Shizu brought Sengyou out of prison, made him acting bearer of the staff, General of Martial Ferocity, and Marquis of Xinxian county, and ordered him to relieve the siege.
translations.idiomatic: In Great Treasure year two Hou Jing raided Jing-Shan and besieged Wang Sengbian at Baling; Shizu freed Sengyou, made him acting staff bearer, General of Martial Ferocity, and Marquis of Xinxian, and sent him to relieve the siege.

sentences.zh: 僧祐將發，謂其子曰：「汝可開兩門，一門擬朱，一門擬白。

translations.literal: As Sengyou was about to set out he told his son: "You may prepare two gates—one gate for red, one gate for white.
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to march he told his son, "Prepare two gates—one for red, one for white.

sentences.zh: 吉則由朱門，凶則由白門。

translations.literal: If fortune comes, enter by the red gate; if misfortune, by the white gate.
translations.idiomatic: If I win, come in by the red gate; if I lose, by the white.

sentences.zh: 吾不捷不歸也。

translations.literal: I shall not return unless victorious."
translations.idiomatic: I will not come home unless I win."

sentences.zh: 」世祖聞而壯之。

translations.literal: When Shizu heard this he admired his spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu heard and was stirred.

sentences.zh: 至楊浦，景遣其將任約率銳卒五千，據白塉，遙以待之。

translations.literal: Reaching Yangpu, Jing sent his general Ren Yue with five thousand crack troops to hold White Embankment, watching for him from afar.
translations.idiomatic: At Yangpu, Jing sent Ren Yue with five thousand elites to hold White Embankment and wait for him.

sentences.zh: 僧祐由別路西上，約謂畏己而退，急追之，及於南安芊口，呼僧祐曰：「吳兒，何爲不早降？

translations.literal: Sengyou took a bypath westward; Yue thought he had feared him and retreated, and pursued urgently; at Nan'an Qian Ford he called to Sengyou: "Wu boy—why do you not surrender early?
translations.idiomatic: Sengyou took a side road west; Yue thought he had fled in fear and chased hard; at Nan'an Qian Ford he shouted to Sengyou, "Wu whelp—why not surrender now?

sentences.zh: 走何處去。

translations.literal: Where will you run?"
translations.idiomatic: Where can you run?"

sentences.zh: 」僧祐不與之言，潛引卻，至赤砂亭，會陸法和至，乃與幷軍擊約，大破之，擒約送于江陵。

translations.literal: " Sengyou did not speak with him but secretly drew back; at Red Sand Pavilion layman Lu Fahe arrived, and together they joined armies and struck Yue, routing him greatly; they captured Yue and sent him to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: " Sengyou would not answer but quietly withdrew; at Red Sand Pavilion Lu Fahe came up, and together they attacked Yue, broke him utterly, captured him, and sent him to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 侯景聞之遂遁。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing heard of it he fled.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing heard and fled.

sentences.zh: 世祖以僧祐爲侍中、領軍將軍，徵還荊州。

translations.literal: Shizu made Sengyou palace attendant and General Who Commands the Army, and summoned him back to Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu made him palace attendant and commanding general and recalled him to Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 承聖二年，進爲車騎將軍、開府儀同三司，餘悉如故。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chengsheng he was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry and Opening-the-Fortress with Three Staffs Equals, all else unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In Chengsheng year two he was promoted General of Chariots and Cavalry and Opening-the-Fortress with Three Staffs Equals; the rest unchanged.

sentences.zh: 西魏寇至，以僧祐爲都督城東諸軍事。

translations.literal: When Western Wei raided, Shizu made Sengyou commander of military affairs east of the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Western Wei attacked, Shizu made him commander east of the city.

sentences.zh: 魏軍四面起攻，百道齊舉，僧祐親當矢石，晝夜督戰，獎勵將士，明於賞罰，衆皆感之，咸爲致死，所向摧殄，賊莫敢前。

translations.literal: Wei armies attacked from all four sides, a hundred routes rising together; Sengyou himself met arrows and stones, supervising battle day and night, rewarding soldiers, clear in reward and punishment—all were moved and fought to the death; wherever he turned he crushed and destroyed; the bandits dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Wei forces assaulted from every side, a hundred lines at once; Sengyou took arrows and stones himself, fighting day and night, clear in rewards and punishments—the men were stirred and died where they stood; nothing could stand before him; the enemy dared not come forward.

sentences.zh: 俄而中流矢卒，時年六十三。

translations.literal: Before long he was struck by a stray arrow and died, aged sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was hit by a stray arrow and died at sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 世祖聞之，馳往臨哭。

translations.literal: When Shizu heard, he raced to attend and weep over the corpse.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu heard and rushed to mourn over the body.

sentences.zh: 於是內外惶駭，城遂陷。

translations.literal: Thereupon inside and outside were terrified and alarmed, and the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: Inside and outside panicked, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 徐文盛，字道茂，彭城人也。

translations.literal: Xu Wensheng, styled Daomao, was a man of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wensheng, styled Daomao, was from Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 世仕魏爲將。

translations.literal: For generations his family served Wei as generals.
translations.idiomatic: His family had served Wei as generals for generations.

sentences.zh: 父慶之，天監初，率千餘人自北歸款，未至道卒。

translations.literal: His father Qingzhi, at the beginning of Heavenly Surveillance, led more than a thousand men to surrender from the north but died on the road before arriving.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qingzhi, early in Heavenly Surveillance, led over a thousand men south to defect but died on the way.

sentences.zh: 文盛仍統其衆，稍立功績，高祖甚優寵之。

translations.literal: Wensheng then took command of his force, gradually achieved merit, and Gaozu favored him exceedingly.
translations.idiomatic: Wensheng took over the troops, won merit step by step, and Gaozu favored him greatly.

sentences.zh: 大同末，以爲持節、督寧州刺史。

translations.literal: At the end of Great Unity he was made bearer of the staff and inspector of Ning prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Great Unity he became staff bearer and inspector of Ning.

sentences.zh: 先是，州在僻遠，所管羣蠻不識教義，貪欲財賄，劫篡相尋，前後刺史莫能制。

translations.literal: Earlier the prefecture lay in remote borderland; the tribal barbarians it governed knew no civil teaching, coveted bribes and goods, and plundered one another in succession—no former inspector could control them.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture was remote; the tribes knew no law, only greed and raiding—no earlier governor had controlled them.

sentences.zh: 文盛推心撫慰，示以威德，夷獠感之，風俗遂改。

translations.literal: Wensheng opened his heart to soothe them, showed them might and virtue; the Yi and Liao were moved, and custom was reformed.
translations.idiomatic: Wensheng won them with sincerity and awed them with strength; the tribes were moved and manners changed.

sentences.zh: 太清二年，聞國難，乃召募得數萬人來赴。

translations.literal: In the second year of Supreme Clarity, hearing of the state's calamity, he mustered and recruited several tens of thousands to come to the relief.
translations.idiomatic: In Supreme Clarity year two, hearing the capital was in peril, he raised tens of thousands and marched east.

sentences.zh: 世祖嘉之，以爲持節、散騎常侍、左衛將軍、督梁、南秦、沙、東益、巴、北巴六州諸軍事、仁威將軍、秦州刺史，授以東討之略。

translations.literal: Shizu praised this and made him bearer of the staff, regular palace attendant, Left Guard general, commander of military affairs in Liang, South Qin, Sha, East Yi, Ba, and North Ba—six prefectures—General of Benevolent Might, and inspector of Qin prefecture, entrusting him with the eastern campaign plan.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu praised him and made him staff bearer, palace attendant, Left Guard general, commander of six prefectures' forces, General of Benevolent Might, and Qin inspector, with the eastern campaign plan.

sentences.zh: 於是文盛督衆軍東下，至武昌，遇侯景將任約，遂與相持。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wensheng led the armies east; reaching Wuchang he met Hou Jing's general Ren Yue and locked in stalemate.
translations.idiomatic: Wensheng led his host east; at Wuchang he met Ren Yue and stood locked.

sentences.zh: 久之，世祖又命護軍將軍尹悅、平東將軍杜幼安、巴州刺史王珣等會之，並受文盛節度。

translations.literal: After a long while Shizu again ordered Protector of the Army Yin Yue, Pacifying East general Du You'an, Ba prefecture governor Wang Xun and others to join him, all under Wensheng's command.
translations.idiomatic: After long delay Shizu sent Yin Yue, Du You'an, Wang Xun, and others to join him, all under Wensheng.

sentences.zh: 擊任約於貝磯，約大敗，退保西陽。

translations.literal: They struck Ren Yue at Shell Ford; Yue was greatly defeated and withdrew to hold Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: They fought Ren Yue at Shell Ford; Yue was routed and fell back on Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 文盛進據蘆洲，又與相持。

translations.literal: Wensheng advanced and held Reed Islet, again in stalemate.
translations.idiomatic: Wensheng took Reed Islet and faced him again.

sentences.zh: 侯景聞之，乃率大衆西上援約，至西陽。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing heard, he led a great host west to relieve Yue, reaching Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing heard and led a great force west to save Yue, reaching Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 文盛不敢戰。

translations.literal: Wensheng did not dare fight.
translations.idiomatic: Wensheng would not give battle.

sentences.zh: 諸將咸曰：「景水軍輕進，又甚饑疲，可因此擊之，必大捷。

translations.literal: The generals all said: "Jing's river army advanced lightly and is very hungry and weary—we can strike now and surely win a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: The generals said, "Jing's fleet came fast and is starving—we can strike now and win a great victory.

sentences.zh: 」文盛不許。

translations.literal: " Wensheng did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: " Wensheng refused.

sentences.zh: 文盛妻石氏，先在建鄴，至是，景載以還之。

translations.literal: Wensheng's wife the Lady Shi had been in Jiankang; at this time Jing conveyed her back to him.
translations.idiomatic: Wensheng's wife Lady Shi had been in Jiankang; Jing now sent her back to him.

sentences.zh: 文盛深德景，遂密通信使，都無戰心，衆咸憤怨。

translations.literal: Wensheng felt deep obligation to Jing and then secretly exchanged envoys; he had no will to fight at all—the host was furious and resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Wensheng felt beholden to Jing and began secret correspondence; he would not fight—the army seethed with anger.

sentences.zh: 杜幼安、守簉等乃率所領獨進，與景戰，大破之，獲其舟艦以歸。

translations.literal: Du You'an, the garrison officer Shouzao and others then led their detachments forward alone, fought Jing, and routed him greatly, capturing his boats and returning.
translations.idiomatic: Du You'an, Shouzao, and others led their men out alone, fought Jing, smashed him, and brought back his ships.

sentences.zh: 會景密遣騎從間道襲陷郢州，軍中兇懼，遂大潰。

translations.literal: Just then Jing secretly sent cavalry by a hidden path to raid and seize E prefecture; the army was panic-stricken and utterly routed.
translations.idiomatic: Then Jing sent cavalry by a hidden road, took E prefecture, and the army collapsed in terror.

sentences.zh: 文盛奔還荊州，世祖仍以爲城北面都督。

translations.literal: Wensheng fled back to Jingzhou; Shizu still made him commander of the north face of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Wensheng fled to Jingzhou; Shizu still made him commander of the north wall.

sentences.zh: 又聚贓汚甚多，世祖大怒，下令責之，數其十罪，除其官爵。

translations.literal: He had also amassed much corrupt booty; Shizu was greatly angered, issued orders to reproach him, counted his ten crimes, and stripped rank and title.
translations.idiomatic: He had also piled up loot; Shizu raged, rebuked him, listed ten crimes, and stripped his titles.

sentences.zh: 文盛旣失兵權，私懷怨望，世祖聞之，乃以下獄。

translations.literal: Having lost military authority, he harbored private resentment; when Shizu heard, he was thrown into prison.
translations.idiomatic: Stripped of command, he nursed grievance; Shizu heard and jailed him.

sentences.zh: 時任約被擒，與文盛同禁。

translations.literal: At the time Ren Yue had been captured and was imprisoned with Wensheng.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yue had been captured and shared his cell.

sentences.zh: 文盛謂約曰：「汝何不早降，令我至此。

translations.literal: Wensheng said to Yue: "Why did you not surrender early and put me in this plight?
translations.idiomatic: Wensheng said to Yue, "Why did you not surrender sooner and spare me this?

sentences.zh: 」約曰：「門外不見卿馬跡，使我何遽得降？

translations.literal: " Yue said: "Outside the gate one saw no trace of your horses—how was I to surrender at once?
translations.idiomatic: " Yue said, "I saw no hoofprints of yours outside the gate—how could I surrender so soon?

sentences.zh: 」文盛無以答，遂死獄中。

translations.literal: " Wensheng had nothing to answer and died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: " Wensheng had no reply and died in prison.

sentences.zh: 杜崱，京兆杜陵人也。

translations.literal: Du Ze, of Dulings in Jingzhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Du Ze was from Dulings in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 其先自北歸南，居於雍州之襄陽，子孫因家焉。

translations.literal: His ancestors had returned south from the north and settled at Xiangyang in Yong province; descendants made their home there.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears came south from the north and settled at Xiangyang in Yong; the family remained there.

sentences.zh: 祖靈啓，齊給事中。

translations.literal: Grandfather Lingqi served Qi as attendant within the court.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Lingqi was a Qi court attendant.

sentences.zh: 父懷寶，少有志節，常邀際會。

translations.literal: Father Huaibao from youth had resolve and integrity, always awaiting the right moment.
translations.idiomatic: His father Huaibao had spirit and principle from youth and waited for his hour.

sentences.zh: 高祖義師東下，隨南平王偉留鎮襄陽。

translations.literal: When Gaozu's righteous army marched east, he followed Prince of Nanping Wei remaining to garrison Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu's army marched east he stayed with Prince of Nanping Wei to hold Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 天監中，稍立功績，官至驍猛將軍、梁州刺史。

translations.literal: In Heavenly Surveillance he gradually achieved merit and reached General of Fierce Valor and inspector of Liang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Under Heavenly Surveillance he rose through merit to General of Fierce Valor and Liang inspector.

sentences.zh: 大同初，魏梁州刺史元羅舉州內附，懷寶復進督華州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Great Unity Wei inspector of Liang Yuan Luo surrendered the prefecture inward; Huaibao was further made superintending commander of Hua prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Great Unity Yuan Luo, Wei inspector of Liang, surrendered; Huaibao was also made commander of Hua.

sentences.zh: 值秦州所部武興氐王楊紹反，懷寶擊破之。

translations.literal: Qin prefecture's dependent Wu Xing had Di king Yang Zhao rebel; Huaibao defeated and broke him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhao, Di king of Wu Xing in Qin, rebelled; Huaibao defeated him.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒於鎮。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died at his post.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he died in office.

sentences.zh: 崱卽懷寶第七子也。

translations.literal: Ze was Huaibao's seventh son.
translations.idiomatic: Ze was Huaibao's seventh son.

sentences.zh: 幼有志氣，居鄉里以膽勇稱。

translations.literal: From youth he had fighting spirit and was known in his hometown for courage and daring.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he had nerve and was known at home for boldness.

sentences.zh: 釋褐廬江驃騎府中兵參軍。

translations.literal: On leaving the office he became army recorder in the Rapid Cavalry command of Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: He began as army recorder on the Lujiang Rapid Cavalry staff.

sentences.zh: 世祖臨荊州，仍參幕府，後爲新興太守。

translations.literal: When Shizu governed Jingzhou he still served on his staff, later becoming governor of Xinxing.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu held Jingzhou he served on his staff, later becoming governor of Xinxing.

sentences.zh: 太清二年，隨岳陽王來襲荊州，世祖以與之有舊，密邀之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Supreme Clarity he followed the Prince of Yueyang in coming to raid Jingzhou; Shizu, having old ties with him, secretly invited him.
translations.idiomatic: In Supreme Clarity year two he came with the Prince of Yueyang to attack Jingzhou; Shizu, who knew him of old, secretly called him over.

sentences.zh: 崱乃與兄岸、弟幼安、兄子龕等夜歸于世祖，世祖以爲持節、信威將軍、武州刺史。

translations.literal: Ze then with his elder brother An, younger brother You'an, and nephew Kan by night returned to Shizu; Shizu made him bearer of the staff, General of Trustworthy Might, and inspector of Wu prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ze came by night with his brother An, younger brother You'an, and nephew Kan; Shizu made him staff bearer, General of Trustworthy Might, and Wu inspector.

sentences.zh: 俄遷宣毅將軍，領鎮蠻護軍、武陵內史，枝江縣侯，邑千戶。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred General Who Chastises the Yi, concurrently Barbarian-quelling Protector, interior minister of Wuling, and Marquis of Zhijiang with a fief of a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became General Who Chastises the Yi, Barbarian-quelling Protector, interior minister of Wuling, and Marquis of Zhijiang with a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 令隨王僧辯東討侯景。

translations.literal: He was ordered to follow Wang Sengbian east to campaign against Hou Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to follow Wang Sengbian east against Hou Jing.

sentences.zh: 至巴陵，會景來攻，數十日不剋而遁。

translations.literal: Reaching Baling, Jing came to attack; for many days he could not take it and fled.
translations.idiomatic: At Baling Hou Jing attacked; after many days he could not win and fled.

sentences.zh: 加侍中、左衛將軍，進爵爲公，增邑五百戶。

translations.literal: He was added palace attendant and Left Guard general, promoted in rank to duke, fief increased five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was made palace attendant and Left Guard general, raised to duke, fief increased five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 仍隨僧辯追景至石頭，與賊相持橫嶺。

translations.literal: He still followed Sengbian pursuing Jing to Stonehead, stalemate with the bandit at Heng Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Sengbian in pursuit to Stonehead and faced the bandit at Heng Ridge.

sentences.zh: 及戰，景親率精銳，左右衝突，崱從嶺後橫截之，景乃大敗，東奔晉陵，崱入據城。

translations.literal: In battle Jing personally led elites, charging left and right; Ze cut in from behind the ridge and Jing was greatly defeated, fleeing east to Jinling; Ze entered and held the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the fight Jing led his best men in person; Ze struck from behind the ridge; Jing was shattered and fled east to Jinling; Ze took the city.

sentences.zh: 景平，加散騎常侍、持節、督江州諸軍事、江州刺史，增邑千戶。

translations.literal: When Jing was pacified he was added regular palace attendant, bearer of the staff, commander of Jiang military affairs, inspector of Jiang—fief increased a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing fell he was added palace attendant, staff bearer, Jiang commander, and Jiang inspector—fief increased a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 是月，齊將郭元建攻秦州刺史嚴超遠於秦郡，王僧辯令崱赴援。

translations.literal: That month Qi general Guo Yuanjian attacked Qin prefecture inspector Yan Chaoyuan at Qin commandery; Wang Sengbian ordered Ze to relieve him.
translations.idiomatic: That month Qi general Guo Yuanjian besieged Yan Chaoyuan at Qin; Wang Sengbian sent Ze to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 陳霸先亦自歐陽來會，與元建大戰于士林，霸先令強弩射，元建衆卻。

translations.literal: Chen Baxian also came from Ouyang to join; with Yuanjian they fought a great battle at Shilin; Baxian ordered strong crossbowmen to shoot and Yuanjian's host withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Baxian came from Ouyang to join; at Shilin they fought Guo Yuanjian; Baxian ordered heavy crossbows and Yuanjian's men fell back.

sentences.zh: 崱因縱兵擊，大破之，斬首萬餘級，生擒千餘人，元建收餘衆而遁。

translations.literal: Ze then released his troops to strike, routing them greatly—more than ten thousand heads cut, more than a thousand captured alive; Yuanjian gathered the remnant and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Ze charged and broke them—ten thousand heads, a thousand prisoners; Yuanjian gathered what was left and fled.

sentences.zh: 時世祖執王琳於江陵，其長史陸納等遂于長沙反，世祖徵崱與王僧辯討之。

translations.literal: At the time Shizu held Wang Lin at Jiangling; his chief clerk Lu Na and others then rebelled at Changsha; Shizu summoned Ze and Wang Sengbian to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu held Wang Lin at Jiangling; Lu Na rebelled at Changsha; Shizu called Ze and Wang Sengbian to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 承聖二年，及納等戰於車輪，大敗，陷其二壘，納等走保長沙，崱等圍之。

translations.literal: In Chengsheng year two they fought Na and others at Wheel Ford, were greatly victorious, took two of their forts; Na and others fled to hold Changsha; Ze and the others besieged them.
translations.idiomatic: In Chengsheng year two they fought Lu Na at Wheel Ford, took two forts, and drove him to Changsha; Ze besieged the city.

sentences.zh: 後納等降，崱又與王僧辯西討武陵王於硤口，至卽破平之。

translations.literal: Later Na and others surrendered; Ze again with Wang Sengbian campaigned west against the Prince of Wuling at Gorge Mouth—reaching there they broke and pacified him at once.
translations.idiomatic: When Na surrendered Ze went west with Wang Sengbian against the Prince of Wuling at Gorge Mouth and broke him at once.

sentences.zh: 於是旋鎮，遘疾卒。

translations.literal: Thereupon he returned to his command but met illness and died.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to his post, fell ill, and died.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「崱，京兆舊姓，元凱苗裔。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Ze—of the old surname of Jingzhao, descendant of Yuan Kai.
translations.idiomatic: The edict said, "Ze, of the ancient house of Jingzhao, line of Yuan Kai.

sentences.zh: 家傳學業，世載忠貞。

translations.literal: His family transmitted learning; generation after generation bore loyal fidelity.
translations.idiomatic: His clan carried learning; generation after generation served in loyalty.

sentences.zh: 自驅傳江渚，政號廉能。

translations.literal: From driving the relay-chariot on the river isles, his rule was called incorrupt and able.
translations.idiomatic: From service on the river isles his rule was called clean and capable.

sentences.zh: 推轂淺原，實聞清靜。

translations.literal: Pushing the chariot-wheel on the shallow ford, one truly heard of his quiet governance.
translations.idiomatic: On the shallow fords of command one heard only of his quiet rule.

sentences.zh: 奄致殞喪，惻愴于懷。

translations.literal: Suddenly he met ruin and death—grief pierces the breast.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly he is gone—grief pierces the heart.

sentences.zh: 可贈車騎將軍，加鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: He may be posthumously made General of Chariots and Cavalry, with one suite of martial music added.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be posthumously made General of Chariots and Cavalry, with martial music.

sentences.zh: 諡曰武。」

translations.literal: His posthumous title shall be Martial."
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous title: Martial."

sentences.zh: 崱兄弟九人，兄嵩、岑、嵸、岌、嶷、巘、岸及弟幼安，並知名當世。

translations.literal: Ze had nine brothers—elder brothers Song, Cen, Cong, Ji, Yi, Yan and An, and younger brother You'an—all famous in their day.
translations.idiomatic: Ze had nine brothers—Song, Cen, Cong, Ji, Yi, Yan, An, and the younger You'an—all famed in their time.

sentences.zh: 岸，字公衡。

translations.literal: An, styled Gongheng.
translations.idiomatic: An, styled Gongheng.

sentences.zh: 少有武幹，好從橫之術。

translations.literal: From youth he had martial capacity and loved schemes of alliance and pressure.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he had martial talent and loved bold stratagems.

sentences.zh: 太清中，與崱同歸世祖，世祖以爲持節、平北將軍、北梁州刺史，封江陵縣侯，邑一千戶。

translations.literal: In Supreme Clarity he returned with Ze to Shizu; Shizu made him bearer of the staff, Pacifying North general, inspector of North Liang, Marquis of Jiangling, fief a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In Supreme Clarity he returned with Ze; Shizu made him staff bearer, Pacifying North general, North Liang inspector, and Marquis of Jiangling with a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 岸因請襲襄陽，世祖許之。

translations.literal: An thereupon requested to raid Xiangyang; Shizu granted it.
translations.idiomatic: An asked to strike Xiangyang; Shizu agreed.

sentences.zh: 岸乃晝夜兼行，先往攻其城，不剋。

translations.literal: He marched day and night, first going to attack the city—but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: He marched day and night and struck the city first—but could not take it.

sentences.zh: 岳陽至，遂走依其兄巘于南陽，巘時爲南陽太守。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yueyang arrived he fled to rely on his brother Yan at Nanyang—Yan was then governor of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yueyang came he fled to his brother Yan at Nanyang, who was then Nanyang governor.

sentences.zh: 岳陽尋遣攻陷其城，岸及巘俱遇害。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yueyang soon sent troops to take the city; An and Yan both met disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The prince soon took the city; An and Yan both perished.

sentences.zh: 幼安性至孝，寬厚，雄勇過人。

translations.literal: You'an was utterly filial by nature, generous and mild, and surpassed others in fierce courage.
translations.idiomatic: You'an was deeply filial, open-handed and mild, yet fiercer than most in battle.

sentences.zh: 太清中，與兄崱同歸世祖，世祖以爲雲麾將軍、西荊州刺史，封華容縣侯，邑一千戶。

translations.literal: In Supreme Clarity he returned with his brother Ze to Shizu; Shizu made him Cloud Banner general, inspector of West Jing, Marquis of Huarong, fief a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In Supreme Clarity he returned with Ze; Shizu made him Cloud Banner general, West Jing inspector, and Marquis of Huarong with a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 令與平南將軍王僧辯討河東王譽於長沙，平之。

translations.literal: He was ordered with Pacifying South general Wang Sengbian to campaign against the Prince of Hedong Yu at Changsha and pacify him.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered with Wang Sengbian to campaign against the Prince of Hedong at Changsha and pacify him.

sentences.zh: 又命率精甲一萬，助左衛將軍徐文盛東討侯景。

translations.literal: He was also ordered to lead ten thousand picked armored troops to aid Left Guard general Xu Wensheng in the eastern campaign against Hou Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He was also told to lead ten thousand armored men to aid Xu Wensheng against Hou Jing.

sentences.zh: 至貝磯，遇景將任約來逆，遂與戰，大敗之。

translations.literal: Reaching Shell Ford he met Jing's general Ren Yue coming to resist; they fought and routed him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: At Shell Ford he met Ren Yue; they fought and broke him.

sentences.zh: 斬其儀同叱羅子通、湘州刺史趙威方等，傳首江陵。

translations.literal: They beheaded his Staff Equal Chiluo Zitong, Xiangzhou inspector Zhao Weifang and others, and sent the heads to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: They cut off Chiluo Zitong, Zhao Weifang of Xiangzhou, and others, and sent the heads to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 乃進軍大舉，因與景相持。

translations.literal: Thereupon the army advanced in force and stalemate with Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Then the host pushed forward and faced Jing in stalemate.

sentences.zh: 別攻武昌，拔之。

translations.literal: Separately he attacked Wuchang and took it.
translations.idiomatic: He also attacked Wuchang and took it.

sentences.zh: 景渡蘆洲上流以壓文盛等，幼安與衆軍攻之，景大敗，盡獲其舟艦。

translations.literal: Jing crossed upstream of Reed Islet to press Wensheng and the others; You'an with the host attacked and Jing was greatly defeated, all his boats captured.
translations.idiomatic: Jing moved above Reed Islet to crush Wensheng; You'an attacked with the army, shattered Jing, and seized every ship.

sentences.zh: 會景密遣襲陷郢州，執刺史方諸等以歸，人情大駭，徐文盛由漢口遁歸，衆軍大敗，幼安遂降于景。

translations.literal: Just then Jing secretly sent a raid that seized E prefecture, capturing inspector Fang Zhu and others and returning; morale was greatly shaken; Xu Wensheng fled by Hankou; the armies were utterly routed; You'an then surrendered to Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Then Jing sent raiders by a hidden road, took E prefecture, and captured Fang Zhu; panic spread; Wensheng fled up the Han; the army collapsed; You'an surrendered to Jing.

sentences.zh: 景殺之，以其多反覆故也。

translations.literal: Jing killed him—for his many vacillations.
translations.idiomatic: Jing killed him for his repeated betrayals.

sentences.zh: 龕，崱第二兄岑之子。

translations.literal: Kan was son of Ze's second elder brother Cen.
translations.idiomatic: Kan was son of Ze's second brother Cen.

sentences.zh: 少驍勇，善用兵，亦太清中與諸父同歸世祖，世祖以爲持節、忠武將軍、鄖州刺史，中廬縣侯，邑一千戶。

translations.literal: From youth fierce and brave, skilled at using troops; also in Supreme Clarity he returned with his uncles to Shizu; Shizu made him bearer of the staff, General of Loyal Martial, inspector of Yun, Marquis of Zhonglu, fief a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was fierce and knew war; in Supreme Clarity he returned with his uncles; Shizu made him staff bearer, General of Loyal Martial, Yun inspector, and Marquis of Zhonglu with a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 與叔幼安俱隨王僧辯討河東王，平之。

translations.literal: With his uncle You'an he followed Wang Sengbian to campaign against the Prince of Hedong and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: With his uncle You'an he followed Wang Sengbian against the Prince of Hedong and pacified him.

sentences.zh: 又隨僧辯下，繼徐文盛軍至巴陵，聞侯景襲陷郢州，西上將至，乃與僧辯等守巴陵以待之。

translations.literal: Again following Sengbian downstream he continued Xu Wensheng's army to Baling; hearing Hou Jing had raided and seized E prefecture and was coming west, he with Sengbian and the others held Baling to await him.
translations.idiomatic: Following Sengbian downriver he took over Wensheng's line at Baling; hearing Jing had taken E and was coming west, he and Sengbian held Baling to meet him.

sentences.zh: 景至，圍之數旬，不剋而遁。

translations.literal: When Jing arrived he besieged it many weeks, could not take it, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Jing besieged it for weeks, failed, and fled.

sentences.zh: 遷太府卿、安北將軍、督定州諸軍事、定州刺史，加通直散騎常侍，增邑五百戶。

translations.literal: He was transferred Grand Treasurer, Pacifying North general, commander of Ding military affairs, inspector of Ding, added Direct and Regular Palace Attendant, fief increased five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He became Grand Treasurer, Pacifying North general, Ding commander and inspector, Direct and Regular Palace Attendant, fief up five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 仍隨僧辯追景至江夏，圍其城。

translations.literal: He still followed Sengbian pursuing Jing to Jiangxia and besieged the city.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Sengbian in pursuit to Jiangxia and besieged the city.

sentences.zh: 景將宋子仙棄城遁，龕追至楊浦，生擒之。

translations.literal: Jing's general Song Zixian abandoned the city and fled; Kan pursued to Yangpu and captured him alive.
translations.idiomatic: Song Zixian abandoned the city and fled; Kan chased to Yangpu and took him alive.

sentences.zh: 大寶三年，衆軍至姑孰，景將侯子鑒逆戰，龕與陳霸先、王琳等率精銳擊之，大敗子鑒，遂至於石頭。

translations.literal: In the third year of Great Treasure the armies reached Gushu; Jing's general Hou Zijian met them in battle; Kan with Chen Baxian, Wang Lin and others led crack troops to strike, routing Zijian greatly, and reached Stonehead.
translations.idiomatic: In Great Treasure year three the armies reached Gushu; Hou Zijian met them; Kan with Chen Baxian and Wang Lin led elites, broke Zijian, and pushed on to Stonehead.

sentences.zh: 景親率其黨會戰，龕與衆軍奮擊，大破景，景遂東奔。

translations.literal: Jing personally led his faction to join battle; Kan with the armies fought fiercely, routing Jing greatly; Jing fled east.
translations.idiomatic: Jing fought in person; Kan and the host struck hard, shattered him, and Jing fled east.

sentences.zh: 論功爲最，授平東將軍、東揚州刺史，益封一千戶。

translations.literal: For merit he was first; he was made Pacifying East general, inspector of East Yang, fief increased a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: His merit ranked first; he was made Pacifying East general, East Yang inspector, fief up a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 承聖二年，又與王僧辯討陸納等於長沙，降之。

translations.literal: In Chengsheng year two he again with Wang Sengbian suppressed Lu Na and others at Changsha and made them surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In Chengsheng year two he again followed Wang Sengbian against Lu Na at Changsha and forced surrender.

sentences.zh: 又征武陵王於西陵，亦平之。

translations.literal: Again he campaigned against the Prince of Wuling at Xiling and likewise pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: He also campaigned against the Prince of Wuling at Xiling and pacified him.

sentences.zh: 後江陵陷，齊納貞陽侯以紹梁嗣，以龕爲震州刺史、吳興太守。

translations.literal: Later Jiangling fell; Qi installed the True Yang Marquis to continue Liang; Kan was made inspector of Zhen and governor of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiangling fell Qi set up the True Yang Marquis to continue Liang; Kan became Zhen inspector and Wuxing governor.

sentences.zh: 又除鎮南將軍、都督南豫州諸軍事、南豫州刺史、溧陽縣侯，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: Also made Pacifying South general, commander of South Yu military affairs, inspector of South Yu, Marquis of Liyang, given a suite of martial music.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made Pacifying South general, South Yu commander and inspector, Marquis of Liyang, with martial music.

sentences.zh: 又加散騎常侍、鎮東大將軍。

translations.literal: Also added Regular Palace Attendant and Great General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made Regular Palace Attendant and Great General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 會陳霸先襲陷京師，執王僧辯殺之。

translations.literal: Just then Chen Baxian raided and seized the capital, seized Wang Sengbian and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Then Chen Baxian seized the capital, took Wang Sengbian, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 龕，僧辯之婿也，爲吳興太守。

translations.literal: Kan, Sengbian's son-in-law, was governor of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Kan was Sengbian's son-in-law and governor of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 以霸先旣非貴素，兵又猥雜，在軍府日，都不以霸先經心；

translations.literal: Because Baxian was neither noble by birth nor his troops were crude and mixed, in headquarters days Kan never took Baxian to heart;
translations.idiomatic: Baxian was low-born and his troops were a rabble; in headquarters days Kan never took him seriously;

sentences.zh: 及爲本郡，每以法繩其宗門，無所縱捨，霸先銜之切齒。

translations.literal: when he became governor of his home commandery he constantly bound his clan by law without indulgence—Baxian hated him to the teeth.
translations.idiomatic: as home governor he bound his clan by law without mercy—Baxian hated him to the bone.

sentences.zh: 及僧辯敗，龕乃據吳興以距之，遣軍副杜泰攻陳蒨於長城，反爲蒨所敗。

translations.literal: When Sengbian was defeated Kan then held Wuxing to resist him, sending deputy Du Tai to attack Chen Qian at Changcheng—but was in turn defeated by Qian.
translations.idiomatic: When Sengbian fell Kan held Wuxing against him and sent Du Tai to strike Chen Qian at Changcheng—but Qian beat him.

sentences.zh: 霸先乃遣將周文育討龕，龕令從弟北叟出距，又爲文育所破，走義興，霸先親率衆圍之。

translations.literal: Baxian then sent general Zhou Wenyun to campaign against Kan; Kan sent his cousin Beisou out to resist and was again broken by Wenyun; he fled to Yixing and Baxian personally led troops to besiege him.
translations.idiomatic: Baxian sent Zhou Wenyun against him; Kan sent his cousin Beisou out and was beaten again; he fled to Yixing and Baxian besieged him in person.

sentences.zh: 會齊將柳達摩等襲京師，霸先恐，遂還與齊人連和。

translations.literal: Just then Qi general Liu Damo and others raided the capital; Baxian was afraid and returned to ally with the Qi men.
translations.idiomatic: Then Liu Damo of Qi struck the capital; Baxian feared and turned back to treat with Qi.

sentences.zh: 龕聞齊兵還，乃降，遂遇害。

translations.literal: When Kan heard the Qi army had withdrawn he surrendered and then met disaster.
translations.idiomatic: When Kan heard Qi had withdrawn he surrendered—and was killed.

sentences.zh: 陰子春，字幼文，武威姑臧人也。

translations.literal: Yin Zichun, styled Youwen, was a man of Guzang in Wuwei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zichun, styled Youwen, was from Guzang in Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 晉義熙末，曾祖襲，隨宋高祖南遷，至南平，因家焉。

translations.literal: At the end of Yixi in Jin, his great-grandfather Xi followed Song Gaozu south, reaching Nanping, and there made home.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Jin Yixi his great-grandfather Xi followed Song Gaozu south to Nanping and settled there.

sentences.zh: 父智伯，與高祖鄰居，少相友善，嘗入高祖臥內，見有異光成五色，因握高祖手曰：「公後必大貴，非人臣也。

translations.literal: Father Zhibo was Gaozu's neighbor; from youth they were friendly; he once entered Gaozu's sleeping chamber and saw a strange light in five colors; he grasped Gaozu's hand and said: "Your Grace will surely rise to great nobility—not the lot of a subject.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhibo lived next to Gaozu; they were friends from youth; once he entered Gaozu's bedchamber and saw a five-colored light; he took Gaozu's hand and said, "You are destined for greatness—not the fate of a subject.

sentences.zh: 天下方亂，安蒼生者，其在君乎！

translations.literal: The realm is in disorder; he who settles the black-haired folk—is it not you?
translations.idiomatic: The realm is in chaos; will you not be the one to save the people?

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「幸勿多言。

translations.literal: " Gaozu said: "Pray speak no more.
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozu said, "Say no more.

sentences.zh: 」於是情好轉密，高祖每有求索，如外府焉。

translations.literal: " Thereupon their affection grew still closer; whenever Gaozu had need it was as from an outer treasury.
translations.idiomatic: " Their bond deepened; whenever Gaozu needed anything it was as if he had another treasury.

sentences.zh: 及高祖踐阼，官至梁、秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne he reached inspector of Liang and Qin.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne he rose to inspector of Liang and Qin.

sentences.zh: 子春，天監初，起家宣惠將軍、西陽太守。

translations.literal: Zichun, at the beginning of Heavenly Surveillance, began office as General of Manifest Grace and governor of Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zichun began under Heavenly Surveillance as General of Manifest Grace and Xiyang governor.

sentences.zh: 普通中，累遷至明威將軍、南梁州刺史；

translations.literal: In the Ordinary era he was repeatedly promoted to General of Bright Might and inspector of South Liang;
translations.idiomatic: In the Ordinary era he rose to General of Bright Might and South Liang inspector;

sentences.zh: 又遷信威將軍、都督梁、秦、華三州諸軍事、梁、秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: also transferred General of Trustworthy Might, commander of Liang, Qin, and Hua military affairs, inspector of Liang and Qin.
translations.idiomatic: then General of Trustworthy Might, commander of Liang, Qin, and Hua, and inspector of Liang and Qin.

sentences.zh: 太清二年，討峽中叛蠻，平之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Supreme Clarity he campaigned against rebel barbarians in the gorges and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: In Supreme Clarity year two he put down rebel tribes in the gorges.

sentences.zh: 徵爲左衛將軍，又遷侍中。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Left Guard general, then transferred palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Left Guard general, then made palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 屬侯景亂，世祖令子春隨領軍將軍王僧辯攻邵陵王於郢州，平之。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled Shizu ordered Zichun to follow General Who Commands the Army Wang Sengbian in attacking the Prince of Shaoling at E prefecture and pacifying him.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled Shizu ordered Zichun to follow Wang Sengbian against the Prince of Shaoling at E and pacify him.

sentences.zh: 又與左衛將軍徐文盛東討侯景，至貝磯，與景遇，子春力戰，恒冠諸軍，頻敗景。

translations.literal: Again with Left Guard general Xu Wensheng he campaigned east against Hou Jing; reaching Shell Ford they met Jing; Zichun fought fiercely, always foremost among the armies, repeatedly defeating Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Again with Xu Wensheng he marched east against Hou Jing; at Shell Ford they met Jing; Zichun fought at the fore and beat him again and again.

sentences.zh: 值郢州陷沒，軍遂退敗。

translations.literal: When E prefecture fell the armies then retreated in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: When E prefecture fell the army retreated in rout.

sentences.zh: 大寶二年，卒於江陵。

translations.literal: In the second year of Great Treasure he died at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: In Great Treasure year two he died at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 孫顥，少知名。

translations.literal: His grandson Hao was known from youth.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Hao was known while still young.

sentences.zh: 釋褐奉朝請，歷尚書金部郎。

translations.literal: On leaving office he was Court Attendant on Duty, successively Jin Department director in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He began as Court Attendant on Duty and rose to director of the Jin Department in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 後入周。

translations.literal: Later he entered Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he went over to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 撰《瓊林》二十卷。

translations.literal: He compiled Pavilions in Splendor in twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Pavilions in Splendor in twenty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：胡僧祐勇幹有聞，搴旗破敵者數矣；

translations.literal: The historian says: Hu Sengyou's bravery and capacity were renowned; several times he seized the standard and broke the enemy;
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Hu Sengyou was famed for courage; again and again he took the standard and broke the foe;

sentences.zh: 及捐軀殉節，殞身王事，雖古之忠烈，何以加焉。

translations.literal: when he gave his body and died for his integrity in the king's service—even the loyal martyrs of antiquity—how could they surpass him?
translations.idiomatic: when he gave his life for the throne—even the martyrs of old—who could surpass him?

sentences.zh: 徐文盛始立功績，不能終其成名，爲不義也。

translations.literal: Xu Wensheng at first achieved merit yet could not finish establishing his name—injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wensheng won merit at first yet could not finish his fame—shame.

sentences.zh: 杜崱識機變之理，知向背之宜，加以身屢典軍，頻殄寇逆，勳庸顯著，卒爲中興功臣。

translations.literal: Du Ze knew the principle of timely change and the fitness of turning toward or away; moreover he repeatedly commanded armies and often extinguished rebels and invaders—merit illustrious, dying a great minister of restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Du Ze read the moment and chose the right side; he led armies again and again and crushed rebels—bright merit, a pillar of restoration.

sentences.zh: 義哉！

translations.literal: Righteous indeed!
translations.idiomatic: How righteous!
